lines: d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Walt Valencia is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d41: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d41: 🕯️ Walt Valencia is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: What Walt kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d41: "Walt's gone." Seymour looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Walt." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d41: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Wolfgang blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Tireless Stride (Level 1). You walk like water downhill — no wasted steps, no wasted breath. Every mile costs 15% less.
d41: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Walt Valencia, 41 days. The mantle passes to Wolfgang Siemsen.
d41: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Wolfgang Siemsen, 48 — a postal worker. Their hands know different work now: Beast-calm.
d41: The village's quarrel was with Walt — and Walt is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d41: At the grave, Seymour, Helga, Wilhelm and 2 more speak for Wolfgang — "Walt trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d41: The fire knew Wolfgang before the Codex did — their name already carried weight here.
